target_customer: Elementary school teachers and districts that buy Mystery Science lessons
problem: Elementary teachers lack time and confidence to teach engaging science; Mystery Science provides open-and-go video lessons and activities.
business_model: Freemium to paid school and teacher subscriptions, sold with no salespeople per the YC page

founders.name: Doug Peltz
prior_employers: LePort Schools (science teacher, seven years per an interview summary)
founders.background_notes: Wikipedia infobox lists the school, no degree. Former middle school science teacher.

founders.name: Keith Schacht
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in Discovery Education's release and EdSurge; the YC page lists only Peltz. Background not found in opened sources.

technical_complexity.rationale: Video lessons and a web lesson library; the hard part was content quality and classroom fit, not software.

defensibility.rationale: A library of 300 plus lessons, teacher habit and school adoption created some lock in, but content can be imitated over time.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Discovery Education bought it in 2020 instead of copying it.

market_need_then: Elementary teachers get little science training; the YC page says thousands of schools were sold without a salesperson and EdSurge reported about 4 million students per month by 2020.

branding.name_origin: Wisconsin Public Radio reports Peltz named himself Mystery Doug because he believes the world is full of mysteries; the company name Mystery Science is not explained by a source.
branding.domain_note: Used mysteryscience.com; the YC listing uses mystery.org after the company renamed itself Mystery (explanation company) for the consumer product.

identity.mascot_or_character: Mystery Doug, the on camera host of weekly mini lessons
identity.voice_and_tone: Curious, kid friendly question and answer style

branding.brand_signature: Mystery Doug video mini lessons answering questions kids submit and vote on

rebrands.why: YC listing uses Mystery.org; a 2023 founder post says the consumer product was spun into The Explanation Company

branding.community_and_virality: Kids submitted questions and voted on the next Mystery Doug episode, per a WPR piece; teacher word of mouth drove adoption per the YC description.

brand_strength.rationale: Used in about half of US elementary schools by 2020 with a recognizable host character, though search results were partly crowded by the unrelated Mystery Science Theater 3000.

outcome_analysis: Mystery Science raised about 2.5 million dollars across two reported seed rounds, grew through teacher word of mouth with no salespeople, and reached roughly half of US elementary schools. Discovery Education acquired it in late October 2020 in a deal EdSurge reported at about 140 million dollars, a large multiple of the venture capital raised. A strong teacher founder, a clear need and capital efficiency explain the outcome.
notes: Funding conflicts: EdSurge says 4.5 million dollars in total venture capital (as of 2020); the two rounds above sum to 2.5 million so other rounds are not found. Aggregators give 800K, 5M or 18.5M for other rounds and are unverified, not recorded. The 140 million figure is a reported estimate, not company confirmed. No competitor sources dated near 2017 were found (results were current day comparison blogs), so the list is empty. Discovery's release date 2020-10-30 comes from a search summary; EdSurge dated the article 2020-11-03 and said the deal closed the prior Friday. Company website redirects to about.mystery.org, which was not fetched.
